statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-52490 affects tiffcrop. The full amd64 and arm64 images contain libtiff-dev and libtiffxx6 as separate binary packages, but contain neither libtiff-tools nor tiffcrop.
Debian confirms that src:zlib does not produce the affected contrib/minizip binary packages.
The affected function is an X.509 writing API; HolyClaude services do not call it directly, and the vendor states internal uses are not affected.
No shipped HolyClaude service loads Perl Socket or calls pack_ip_mreq_source; Perl remains an explicit developer tool.
No shipped HolyClaude service evaluates attacker-controlled Perl regular expressions; Perl remains an explicit developer tool.
No shipped HolyClaude service parses EXR IDManifest data; EXR libraries are available only to explicit developer workloads.
No shipped HolyClaude service parses attacker-controlled EXR scanline data; EXR libraries are available only to explicit developer workloads.
No shipped HolyClaude service deserializes attacker-controlled Perl Storable data; Perl remains an explicit developer tool.
The libssh advisory limits this flaw to the OpenSSL backend. HolyClaude's exact Debian package is the Gcrypt build, links libgcrypt, and does not link libcrypto or libssl.
The libssh advisory limits this flaw to libssh 0.11.0 and newer. HolyClaude ships Debian libssh-gcrypt-4 0.10.6.
The libssh advisory limits this flaw to libssh 0.11.0 and newer. HolyClaude ships Debian libssh-gcrypt-4 0.10.6.

Upstream lists versions through 2.42.2 as affected and Debian marks exact Bookworm 2.38.1 source vulnerable. This disposition is limited to the advisory-described privileged post-helper path, which cannot execute because the exact source lacks the post-mount hook framework and X-mount.idmap and owner hooks; it does not declare the version generally unaffected.

CVE-2026-52490 is confined to tools/tiffcrop.c, which Debian builds into the separately packaged tiffcrop executable. The full amd64 image contains libtiff6 but no libtiff-tools or tiffcrop; its real TIFF consumers link libtiff.so.6 without the separately compiled tool code.

The exact Junie 3196.5 nested JAR SHA-256 f82726298a4e12ee3798bcda516fbaf0d9d6b85da89110b7bd62801af64997f7 contains Netty 4.2.9.Final and is bound to the sole manifest-supported standalone Main-Class plus exact command-surface hashes: GatewayServerKt.class 6a1da55c9a946f73d5d5795c1f51a641c712d75fdd5421e852f2ab7a239c5221, gateway MainKt.class 0447ad9e5f7c4e8ebd96bafafa4a2eac81340396e3d03f2692c099b710a55642, standalone MainKt.class bb30e63ba85ace4a353ed4e5036e89232aa7508308f7d690ac002a9731b63869, JunieCli.class f4e40d610438ff9f553ccc6529d943d5272eb8fa26e3c92ae51812623bfee438, SystemOptionsGroup.class 5a953748e13fcd3b0006b007c77616651358522fa4f38a86d7a31ec18c14cf4d. It has no non-Netty SNI references and retains the reviewed Ktor TLS baseline. Acceptance requires the native full amd64 guard to prove stable gateway mode is runtime-disabled with status 1 and the exact stable-channel diagnostic, with no surviving launcher descendant or listener. Embedded private gateway classes remain covered by the static TLS and SNI checks and are not supported entrypoints.
